name: Digikala
description: Digikala combines a broad online shopping platform with services for independent sellers in Iran. Its marketplace connects product discovery, merchant operations, and delivery, while the wider group also operates in logistics, financial technology, and digital content.

seo.title: Digikala: Iran’s Online Retail and Marketplace Platform | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore Digikala’s marketplace, seller services, delivery arrangements, and company-reported annual sales figures, with clear evidence limitations.

content.heading: A marketplace behind the shopping website
content.content:
Digikala is an Iranian online shopping platform whose significance extends beyond the products displayed on its homepage. The consumer website brings together electronics, household goods, clothing, books, and personal-care products. Alongside this shopping interface sits a merchant operation: independent businesses can list products, set prices, manage stock, and handle orders through the platform’s seller tools. Understanding both sides helps explain why Digikala belongs in a discussion of business infrastructure as well as retail. [s1][s2]

The distinction between the shopping platform and the wider Digikala Group also matters. The group describes activities spanning e-commerce, logistics, financial technology, and content. These are connected business areas, but a group-level description should not be read as proof that every service is included in every retail order or available to every merchant. [s3]

content.heading: What the platform offers merchants
content.content:
Digikala’s seller recruitment page describes a workflow of registration, product selection or activation, and order management. Merchants enter prices and inventory information rather than simply handing over an undifferentiated stock of goods. The same page advertises tools for managing orders, stock, pricing, advertising, and sales performance. These functions show how a marketplace can become part of a merchant’s everyday operating system. [s2]

Fulfillment—the work of preparing and delivering an order—is not presented as a single uniform arrangement. The seller page lists delivery by Digikala and delivery by the seller. It also promotes direct shipment through postal and courier services. Consequently, an explanation of Digikala should not assume that every item passes through the same warehouse or follows the same delivery route. These are advertised service arrangements; this research did not test individual seller accounts or delivery outcomes. [s2]

content.heading: Reading annual sales without confusing value and volume
content.content:
The company’s report for Solar Hijri year 1404 includes a short comparison of average annual sales per seller. The observations are reproduced below in their original reporting calendar and monetary denomination. They measure sales value, not seller profit, household income, or the number of products sold. [s4]

The reported average rises across the available observations. That does not establish that a typical merchant experienced the same increase: an average can change when the composition of sellers changes, and nominal monetary growth does not isolate changes in prices from changes in sales volume. The inspected presentation does not provide enough detail about the seller denominator or distribution to resolve those questions. It therefore supports a limited description of the published series rather than a claim about merchant prosperity. [s4]

content.title: Company-reported average annual sales per seller, million Iranian toman

content.heading: Why the model matters
content.content:
Digikala illustrates how online commerce brings together several distinct services: finding customers, maintaining product information, processing merchant operations, and arranging delivery. Its breadth makes those connections visible within a single business ecosystem. For an international reader, the useful question is how these activities fit together, rather than whether a familiar foreign company provides an exact analogy. [s1][s2][s3]

The evidence here establishes the platform’s advertised structure and a narrowly defined financial series. It does not independently establish service quality, market dominance, seller profitability, or equal access across regions.

name: Basalam
description: Basalam is an Iranian online marketplace organized around individual sellers and their digital stalls. Its social-bazaar approach combines product discovery with direct communication between buyers and merchants.

seo.title: Basalam: Iran’s Seller-Led Online Bazaar | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Discover Basalam’s digital stalls, buyer–seller communication, regional business origins, and developer ecosystem, with evidence gaps identified.

content.heading: The digital stall as a business model
content.content:
Basalam brings the idea of a bazaar into an online marketplace. Sellers establish digital stalls, known in Persian as *ghorfeh*, through which they present products and communicate with potential customers. Digiato’s company profile describes this as a social marketplace connecting merchants from across Iran. The emphasis is on identifiable sellers and conversations around products, rather than a shopping experience built only around a centralized catalogue. [s2]

The company’s own homepage reinforces that positioning by advertising direct contact with people, payment through banking gateways, a money-back guarantee, and online and telephone support. These are platform promises, not independently measured outcomes. Together, however, they show the functions Basalam presents as necessary to make transactions between unfamiliar buyers and sellers possible. [s1]

content.heading: Regional origins and a widening product range
content.content:
Digiato dates the marketplace’s launch to Aban 1395 in Iran’s Solar Hijri calendar and places its principal office in Qom. Its account emphasizes an early interest in small businesses in towns and villages, especially products made outside large industrial supply chains. This provides useful context for Basalam’s identity: regional producers and their stories were part of the proposition, rather than incidental additions to a general retailer. [s2]

That origin should not be mistaken for a fixed boundary around the business. The inspected homepage displays a much broader selection, including food, beauty products, household items, and other merchandise. It also links to wholesale and organizational purchasing. A reader should therefore distinguish the marketplace’s small-producer origins from the breadth of commerce presented on the later website. [s1][s2]

content.title: The relationships behind Basalam’s social marketplace
content.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["Seller"] -->|"Operates"| T["Digital stall"]
  T -->|"Displays"| P["Product offer"]
  B["Buyer"] -->|"Discovers"| P
  B -->|"Discusses products with"| S
  M["Basalam platform"] -->|"Hosts"| T
  M -->|"Advertises payment and support services to"| B
```
content.summary: The diagram separates the seller, the seller’s stall, and the platform hosting it. Its arrows describe product discovery, communication, and advertised services; they do not establish legal liability or a universal shipping arrangement.

content.heading: Beyond the storefront
content.content:
Basalam also presents a developer platform called Salam API. An API, or application programming interface, allows software to communicate with a service in a defined way. The inspected developer homepage links to documentation, an API reference, a developer panel, and an app store. It advertises tools for applications, subscriptions, payments, and promotion. These materials indicate an ambition to support software built around the marketplace, although their presence does not establish adoption or commercial success. [s3]

This distinction matters for understanding potential business relationships. Selling merchandise through a stall and building software for merchants are different activities, with different requirements. The developer website documents the latter as a separate part of the ecosystem. Availability before the editorial cutoff, access conditions, technical reliability, and integration costs still require verification. [s3]

content.heading: What this model helps explain
content.content:
Basalam is useful for understanding how regional commerce can be organized around merchant identity and conversation. Its historical profile describes direct seller shipment, while its homepage emphasizes communication and platform support. This combination makes the relationship between buyer, merchant, and intermediary central to the business model. Historical descriptions of fees, settlement, or delivery times should not be treated as current terms. [s1][s2]

The inspected evidence supports an explanation of the model. It does not establish how much additional income sellers earn, whether rural merchants benefit equally, or how consistently disputes are resolved.

name: Khanoumi
description: Khanoumi is an Iranian online retailer centered on beauty, personal care, and related products. Its corporate account describes expansion into business purchasing, industry media, and other services alongside its consumer store.

seo.title: Khanoumi: Beauty and Personal-Care E-commerce in Iran | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: Explore Khanoumi’s specialist retail model, company-reported development, product information, and published return policies.

content.heading: Specialist retail built around beauty
content.content:
Khanoumi is an Iranian online retailer associated with cosmetics, skincare, haircare, fragrance, and personal-care products. Its storefront organizes merchandise into detailed categories, including different kinds of cleansers, moisturizers, makeup, and hair products. This structure illustrates the logic of specialist e-commerce: customers need help navigating distinctions within a product field, not simply access to a large undifferentiated catalogue. [s1]

The website also contains product videos, magazine articles, and selected customer comments. These place editorial and user-generated material beside the shopping journey. Their presence shows how information is incorporated into retail presentation; it does not establish that every product claim or customer account has been independently verified. [s1]

content.heading: From a specialist store to a broader group
content.content:
Khanoumi’s corporate timeline dates its website and Instagram activity to Solar Hijri year 1393. It subsequently records investment, the opening of an order-processing center, and expansion into additional business lines. These are company-reported milestones, useful for understanding how Khanoumi describes its development rather than an independently reconstructed corporate history. [s2]

The same page distinguishes the consumer store from other activities. Khanoumi Bazaar is presented as a business-to-business service connecting wholesale supply and retail purchasing. Khanoumi Business is described as an industry publication, while other divisions concern advertising and brand development. The distinction is practical: a consumer buying skincare, a retailer sourcing stock, and a manufacturer promoting a brand have different relationships with the group. [s2]

content.heading: Authenticity claims and product information
content.content:
In its company profile on LinkedIn, Khanoumi says it sources products from manufacturers or official brand representatives to support authenticity. That statement establishes its declared sourcing approach. It is not an independent certification of every item offered, and this research did not inspect supplier contracts, authorization documents, or product-level testing. [s3]

For international readers, the important distinction is between a retailer’s assurance, the information supplied about a product, and evidence that independently establishes its origin or performance. Khanoumi’s specialist positioning makes those questions central to understanding the business. Claims that it is the first or largest retailer in its field are not adopted here because a dated, independently supported comparison was not established. [s3]

content.heading: Why product categories affect returns
content.content:
Khanoumi’s published return FAQ distinguishes concerns about authenticity, changes of mind, electrical products, and gold. For ordinary changes of mind, its answers emphasize original condition and intact seals. The page also directs customers to coordinate a return with support before sending goods back. These provisions show why a simple promise of returns needs to be read alongside category-specific conditions. [s4]

The wording is not entirely uniform: one answer stresses hygiene restrictions, while another describes returns for sealed goods in their original condition. This page therefore does not reduce the policy to an unconditional guarantee. The FAQ is evidence of the retailer’s published position when inspected, not a legal assessment or proof of how every complaint is handled. [s4]

content.heading: What Khanoumi illustrates
content.content: Khanoumi offers a focused example of commerce organized around a product field, with consumer shopping connected to content and adjacent industry services. Its corporate descriptions suggest a business seeking relationships across supply, promotion, and consumption. Evaluating the results requires more than a catalogue or a milestone timeline: comparable annual operating data and independent evidence of customer and supplier outcomes remain necessary. [s1][s2]
